h: Why a College Zoo Is Worth Your Afternoon
p: Most zoos are run as attractions first and classrooms second. Here it's the other way round, and that's exactly what gives the place its charm. Askham Bryan College has trained farmers, land workers and animal care students for decades, and the wildlife park is part of that teaching. The people looking after the animals are learning their trade, so you'll often find young keepers bursting to tell you about the species they've been studying.

That makes it a lovely fit for children who are animal-mad and already talking about being a vet or a zookeeper when they grow up. It's a chance to see what the job really involves, from enrichment to feeding, and to ask questions without feeling rushed. Smaller children get the simpler joy of being close to animals without the scale and crowds of a huge zoo.

Getting there is straightforward. The college sits just off the A64 ring on the south-west edge of the city, near the village of Askham Bryan, so it's easy by car and avoids the tight city centre streets. The Knavesmire, home to York Racecourse, is on the same side of town if you fancy a stretch of the legs on wide open grass afterwards.

Pack a picnic or plan a lunch back in town. Then make for the walls: walking a section of York's medieval city walls is free and gives cracking views of the Minster, a perfect way to round off a day with the little ones.
